items.title: Lesson Podcast
items.description: Audio guide to animal communication's four limited functions, Von Frisch's bee waggle dance study, and what makes human language unique.

items.title: Language, Thought and Communication: GCSE Psychology (Audio)
items.description: The Psychology Podcast series that includes episodes on animal cognition, language, and comparative communication — useful background listening.

items.title: Why Do Bees Dance? The Bee Dance Study by Karl von Frisch
items.description: Explains Von Frisch's study of honeybee communication and what the waggle dance tells us about animal signalling systems.

items.title: The Waggle Dance of the Honeybee
items.description: Classic educational animation showing how honeybees use waggle and round dances to communicate distance and direction of food sources.

items.title: Two Monkeys Were Paid Unequally | Frans de Waal TED
items.description: Frans de Waal demonstrates fairness and emotional communication in primates — highlights the sophistication and limits of animal signalling.

items.title: Watch Koko the Gorilla Use Sign Language | National Geographic
items.description: 1981 National Geographic footage of Koko the gorilla communicating via American Sign Language, raising questions about animal language acquisition.

items.title: A Conversation With Koko the Gorilla — Full Documentary
items.description: PBS Nature documentary following decades of research with Koko — explores the boundary between animal communication and true language.

items.title: Project Nim (2011)
items.description: Documentary about Nim Chimpsky, the chimpanzee raised as a human child to see if he could acquire language — available on Netflix UK.

items.title: BBC Bitesize — AQA GCSE Psychology
items.description: Bitesize hub with notes and quizzes on human versus animal communication and Von Frisch's bee study for AQA GCSE.
